distinguishing_features: Physical tuned_mass_damper (spring-mass-damper) added to the spindle support structure rather than a monitoring/indication inference scheme
Passive out-of-phase inertial counter-force tuned to the critical speed dissipates stored vibration energy
A structural design change (embedded radial spring ring) rather than signal processing of existing sensors
Tuned to the rotating system's critical speed rather than the static natural frequency of the component
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to suppress self-excited resonance (chatter) at the spindle's critical speed without globally altering the structure's stiffness and thereby shifting all vibrational modes.
parsed.viable_reason: The TMD coordinates given are self-consistent (0.3 kg mass, ~82 kN/m stiffness, ~83 Hz tuning) and the mass/stiffness/damping values are physically realizable with commodity parts, and the acceptance test is runnable.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The prior art is entirely monitoring/indication inference schemes (resonance tracking, phase cross-correlation, film-viscosity prediction); none teaches adding a physical tuned mass damper that provides out-of-phase inertial damping at the critical speed, so this structural departure is not an obvious step from the cited art.
